answer: Each identity moors to one opal anchor on the harbor floor, locks 70 credits, and flies a plume from its buoy. Each epoch a lantern sweep tests every mooring: two identities on one opal, a shared line, or a copied plume burns the bond. First costs 38, the kth 38+6(k-1); 1,000 fakes cost 3,035,000 plus 70,000 locked against a 40,000 pool. A rented mooring still names its lender, so both burn. An honest agent pays 38 once and keeps the full share.
